newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares succumb to light profit taking.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares succumb to light profit taking.

text.p: The New Zealand share market succumbed to profit taking on Monday after hitting record highs last week, brokers said.

Market heavyweight Telecom Corp again appeared immune to selling, however, and closed three cents up at near an all-time high of $7.83. Brokers said institutions remained underweight and had to chase stock to balance portfolios.
The top 40 index closed 12.87 points lower at 2513.78. Volume was light compared to most of last week at $57 million.
Brokers expect the re-entry of U.S. players following the long holiday weekend to boost volumes and provide direction.
"It looks a little soggy but we'll have to wait and see what happens when the offshore markets re-enter," said First NZ Capital's Jim Patterson of the market's direction.
Brierley Investments suffered following a poor performance on Friday of the British hotel sector including its 46 percent-held Thistle Hotels.
Also weak among the leaders were forestry products stocks -- Carter Holt Harvey, dropping five to $3.68 and Fletcher Paper off three to $3.48.

McCraes Mining slid 20 cents to $1.85 as the gold sector in Australia took more punishment while New Zealand Salmon lost a massive 37.5 percent of its value -- down 12 cents to 20 -- after on Friday it reported troubles in its only major investment - the Chilean fishing company Aquacultivos.
